description: The break schedule for one state in one effective period. A data record, not code, for the same reason every other compliance threshold is: regulations do not move on a release cadence, and a number that lives in Python is a number that needs a deploy to change. Oregon renumbered heat illness from -1130 to -1131 mid-stream; Washington's ag heat rule became permanent in 2023 and was amended in 2024.

fields.description: Blank means current — the policy is in effect until replaced.
fields.label: Effective To

fields.description: The statutes and administrative rules this schedule is read from. Kept as text rather than a link because the citation is the evidence, and an evidence record that points at nothing is worse than one that quotes the number.
fields.label: Regulation Citations

fields.description: The person who read each citation against the rule and approved it. Blank until somebody does — a policy with no approver is returned to the handset with approved: false, and the break coach shows a caveat.
fields.label: Approved By
Minor Schedule (under 18)
fields.description: OAR 839-021-0072. A worker under eighteen is owed a rest period every TWO hours and a meal every FOUR, against four and six for an adult under OAR 839-020-0050 — so the entitlement is a different table rather than a multiplier on this one. LEAVING THESE EMPTY IS SAFE AND VISIBLE: a policy with no minor rows computes a minor's entitlement from the adult schedule above, which owes FEWER periods and therefore shows up as a shortfall the moment anybody reads the shift, rather than as a silent exemption.
Rest periods owed a worker under eighteen, by hours worked. Read INSTEAD OF `rest_schedule` for anybody whose `date_of_birth` makes them a minor on the day of the shift — never in addition to it.
fields.label: Minor Rest Schedule

fields.description: Meal periods owed a worker under eighteen, by hours worked. Read INSTEAD OF `meal_schedule` for a minor.
fields.label: Minor Meal Schedule

fields.description: The longest a minor may work without a rest period. Supersedes `max_hours_without_rest` for a minor where it is set, and falls back to it where it is not — the same direction as the two tables above. Zero or empty means the adult ceiling applies.
fields.label: Minor Max Hours Without Rest

fields.description: Washington: no worker may work more than 3 hours without a rest period. Oregon: no hard ceiling. Null rather than a large sentinel, so a client that ignores it produces no countdown rather than a wrong one.
fields.label: Max Hours Without Rest

name: Labor Break Policy
